decision_conditions: <p><span style="font-size:11pt"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif">The retrospective development is unacceptable in terms of highway safety as it is un<span style="line-height:115%">authorised and&nbsp;</span>c<span style="line-height:115%">ontrary to the relevant policies and the legal agreements. It is therefore&nbsp;</span></span></span><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="font-size:11pt">is a breach of planning which could conflict with pedestrian movement and result in unacceptable parking stress thus be&nbsp;</span></span><span style="font-size: 14.6667px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;">detrimental to the&nbsp;public realm and safety of the highway network. Furthermore, if approved, it could&nbsp;</span><span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size:11pt">set an unacceptable precedent.</span></span><span style="font-size: 11pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="line-height:115%">&nbsp;</span></span></span><span style="background-color: rgb(229, 229, 229); font-size: 11pt;"><span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;">&nbsp;</span></span><span style="background-color: rgb(229, 229, 229);">As such, the proposal is contrary to the following policies:&nbsp;</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policy T1, T2, T4 and T6 of the London Plan (March 2021)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policy DMT1 and DMT2 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024</span></li></ul>

<p>The retrospective development&nbsp;<span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 11pt;">is unacceptable in terms of design as it presents a visually intrusive feature that contradicts the conditions that were enforced in the interests of visual amenity.&nbsp;</span><span style="background-color: rgb(229, 229, 229);">As such, the proposal is contrary to the following policies:&nbsp;</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policy&nbsp;D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policy DMD1 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></li></ul>

<p>The retrospective development is not supported in principle as it&nbsp;<span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size:11pt">results in the loss of approved soft landscaping which does not comply with the s106 agreement attached to the original planning permission. Furthermore, it contradicts the relevant policies&nbsp;</span></span><span style="font-size: 11pt;"><span style="font-family:Arial,Helvetica,sans-serif"><span style="line-height:115%">on urban greening, biodiversity, and sustainable drainage&nbsp;</span></span></span><span style="font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;"><span style="font-size:11pt">and the enforceable conditions attached to the original planning permission. Therefore, it is a breach of planning which could set an unacceptable precedent if approved. For these reasons, it&nbsp;</span></span><span style="background-color: rgb(229, 229, 229);">is contrary to the following policies:&nbsp;</span></p><ul><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">National Planning Policy Framework (December 2024)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policies G1, G5 and G6 of the London Plan (March 2021)</span><br></li><li style="text-align: justify;"><span style="font-size: 11pt;">Policies DMNE2 and DMNE3 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham Local Plan 2037 (September 2024)</span></li></ul>
borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
description:
Retrospective application for the installation of an area
of hardstanding for off-street parking in place of the as approved area of
landscaping and proposed removal of on-street parking spaces including addition
of a dropped kerb, a new crossover and soft landscaping, and the removal of existing dropped kerb and
reinstatement of pavement
